name: Honeycomb Launcher
tagline: A home screen of bubbles you can fling, pinch and play with.
description: Honeycomb Launcher replaces your home screen with a honeycomb of round app icons, like a smartwatch. Pan in any direction and the grid never ends, pinch out to see every app at once, and tap a bubble to open it. Favorites slide out from the edge of the screen, and a dock and search are a thumb away. It works on regular phones and on foldables, with a separate setup for each screen.

features.title: Endless honeycomb
features.text: Scroll any way and the grid keeps going. Scroll sideways and the apps flow down the screen one band at a time, so every app passes the middle in one loop.

features.title: Real physics
features.text: Fling the grid, pinch out to a map of every app, or turn on gravity and tilt the phone to pour the bubbles into a pile.

features.title: Favorites drawer
features.text: Swipe in from the side or tap the badge, and your favorite apps fan out under your thumb, with quick buttons for the flashlight, screenshots, Wi-Fi and more.

features.title: Dock, folders and search
features.text: Drag an app onto the dock, hold one bubble over another to make a folder, and type to find any app above the keyboard.

features.title: Your look
features.text: Icon packs, themed monochrome icons, custom icons per app, labels on or off, and sort by name, color, category, most used or install date.

features.title: Idle drift
features.text: Leave the phone alone and the honeycomb glides slowly across a field of stars.

features.title: Games
features.text: Brick breaker, air hockey and bowling, all played with your own app icons. Air hockey has ten levels and a two-player mode.

features.title: Made for foldables
features.text: The cover screen and the inner screen each keep their own layout, and in tabletop mode the controls move below the hinge.

features.title: Light on battery
features.text: Nothing runs while the home screen is hidden, and a still screen draws nothing at all.

setup: Download the file on your phone and open it.
If Android asks, allow your browser to install apps.
Press the Home button and choose Honeycomb, then tap Always.
Long-press an empty spot for Settings, games and sorting.
limits: Lock screen, screenshot, recent apps and the power menu buttons need Honeycomb turned on once under Accessibility. It only presses those buttons and doesn't read your screen.
Recent apps in the dock need Usage access.
Samsung phones play their own animation when an app opens from a third-party home screen.
This is a test build, so Android will warn that it comes from an unknown source.
